title: Khudadad and His Brothers

full_text:
Prince Khudadad of Harran was a youth of peerless martial prowess, raised in seclusion by his noble mother. Arriving at his father the King’s court, his forty-nine half-brothers grew envious of his valor and departed on a reckless adventure into the mountains, where they were all captured and imprisoned in the Black Castle of an immense, cannibalistic giant.

Khudadad tracked them to the mountains, challenged the giant to single combat, and through agile horsemanship and heroic valor, slew the monster, breaking the chains of his forty-nine brothers and liberating the captive Princess of Daryabar!

Instead of thanking him, consuming envy seized the brothers: while Khudadad slept by a stream, they stabbed him and left him for dead, carrying the princess back to court, claiming they had slain the giant themselves!

Recovering from his wounds through the nursing of a friendly hermit, Khudadad returned to Harran just as an invading army of nomads besieged the capital.

Khudadad charged into the fray, routed the enemy, and saved his father’s crown!

Revealing his identity, Khudadad forgave his treacherous brothers before the full council, pleading for their pardon. The King embraced Khudadad, crowned him heir to the throne, and celebrated his union with the heroic Princess of Daryabar.
moral: Chivalric valor, filial loyalty, and boundless fraternal forgiveness conquer the fiercest monsters.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "Khudadad and His Brothers"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.
